provenance_note: Synthetic Bharat-Line-style fleet (PLAN.md §5.4/§6.2) — no real operator's data. 10 vessels: 4 Band A, 3 Band B, 3 Band C, matching docs/scope_matrix.md and PLAN.md §5.4 exactly. Vessel particulars are prototype-grade class defaults (see vessel_class_defaults[*].source), not per-vessel specifics — nothing downstream needs more precision than 'representative of a named public vessel class' for this prototype.

A.source: Panamax containership class: GT ~40,000-50,000, DWT ~65,000-80,000, up to ~25 kn (midpoint figures used here). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panamax ; https://www.marineinsight.com/types-of-ships/what-are-panamax-ships/ (retrieved 2026-08-30).
A.anchor_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — derived from a representative VLSFO-equivalent daily bunker consumption of ~180 t/day at design speed (order-of-magnitude figure for this vessel class, not vessel-specific data) x VLSFO's own lcv_mj_per_tonne (see fuel_properties.vlsfo) = 180 * 41000. Stored as energy, not mass, because mass depends on which fuel is actually burned (Task 2R component 3 correction 1).
A.fixed_opex_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — crew/insurance/maintenance lump sum, order-of-magnitude for this vessel class.
A.charter_premium_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — stated directly rather than computed, to avoid false precision; approximates fixed_opex_usd_per_year/365 (~$9,590/day) plus a charter-hire/opportunity-cost premium for additional time at sea (Task 2R component 3 correction 2).

B.source: Handysize bulk-carrier class — general industry-standard figures (GT ~20,000-28,000, DWT ~35,000, ~14 kn). Not independently re-searched this session beyond the Panamax pass above; flagged for a follow-up citation search if this figure becomes load-bearing beyond the prototype.
B.anchor_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — ~50 t/day VLSFO-equivalent x 41000 MJ/tonne. See Band A's anchor_status for the same derivation logic.
B.charter_premium_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — approximates fixed_opex_usd_per_year/365 (~$4,930/day) plus a charter-hire premium. See Band A's charter_premium_status.

C.source: Small coastal feeder / general-cargo class — general industry-standard figures. Same not-independently-re-searched caveat as Band B. GT deliberately well under the 5,000 GT regulatory threshold (docs/scope_matrix.md Band C).
C.anchor_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — ~8 t/day VLSFO-equivalent x 41000 MJ/tonne. See Band A's anchor_status for the same derivation logic.
C.charter_premium_status: ILLUSTRATIVE — approximates fixed_opex_usd_per_year/365 (~$1,100/day) plus a charter-hire premium. See Band A's charter_premium_status.

routes_status: distance_nm and min_capacity_dwt_required are ILLUSTRATIVE (representative annual transit distance and a one-vessel-worth demand floor for the route-year) — ballparked from general geographic knowledge of the route pairs, not a routing-engine computation.

engine_fuel_compatibility.status: Engineering-compatibility modelling choice, not a regulatory constant — deliberately kept out of regulations.json.

fuel_properties.status: SECONDARY_SOURCE — FuelEU Annex II's actual per-fuel default table could not be extracted this session (paywalled/PDF-only in the sources found); figures below are from general industry knowledge, cross-checked only insofar as the fossil-fuel WtW figures land close to regulations.json's 91.16 gCO2e/MJ 2020 fleet-average baseline (itself HFO/VLSFO/MGO-dominated, so a real if partial consistency check). LNG and methanol LCVs are near-universal engineering constants (higher confidence than the WtW/carbon-intensity column). Flagged for a real Annex II pull before this feeds anything beyond the prototype.

vlsfo.notes: ≈ regulations.json's 2020 fleet-average baseline (91.16), which is dominated by this fuel.

b30_blend.notes: 30% biofuel blended into VLSFO; corrected during Task 2R component 3 review from an earlier, less careful biofuel-component assumption.

methanol.notes: Renewable/green-methanol pathway, matching prices.json's own framing of the methanol option as green rather than grey (fossil) methanol. LCV (~half of conventional fuels) is a well-known, high-confidence figure independent of the carbon-intensity pathway assumption.

shore_power_model.status: ILLUSTRATIVE — global technology/policy parameters, not per-vessel.
